title: Haitian Revolution
summary: In August 1791 enslaved people in northern Saint-Domingue, France's richest colony, began a mass rebellion that grew into a thirteen-year struggle involving free people of colour, planters, and French, Spanish and British forces. It ended in 1804 with the independent state of Haiti, the second independent country in the Americas.

uncertainty.note: The Office of the Historian dates the rebellion to 22 August 1791; the Bois Caiman ceremony is placed in August 1791 by a university text, which notes its details cannot be known. End year 1804 is from the Office of the Historian title; the day of independence was not confirmed on an opened page.

importance.justification: Only successful slave revolt to found a state; reshaped the Atlantic world.

audience_note: Describes a slave revolt and war with heavy civilian suffering, destruction and refugee flight.

related.because: The French Revolution split the colony's white minority and gave the mixed-race population and the enslaved an opening (Office of the Historian).

beats.caption: Enslaved people in northern Saint-Domingue began a massive rebellion.
Rival factions fought for Cap-Francais; the fighting and fire destroyed much of the capital and sent refugees to ports in the United States.
The revolution ended with independent Haiti, the second independent country in the Americas.
